from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Harmonic Oscillator Model", [
            "Electrons act like masses on springs.",
            "Lorentz oscillator shows driving force.",
            "Light wave pushes electrons to oscillate."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use assets
        mass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mass.svg", color='#FFFFFF')
        spring = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/spring.svg", color='#FFD700')
        oscillator_system = VGroup(spring, mass).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(oscillator_system, 'B3', 'D5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.add(oscillator_system)
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FFD700')
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        equilibrium = Circle(radius=0.3, color='#FF00FF').move_to(self.grid['C4'])
        self.play(FadeIn(equilibrium))
        self.play(Flash(equilibrium, color='#FF00FF', line_length=0.2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FF00FF')
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        mass.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(self.grid['C4'] + RIGHT * 0.5 * np.sin(tracker.get_value())))
        
        # Sine wave graph tracking displacement
        light_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x),
            x_range=[-PI, PI],
            color='#00FFFF'
        )
        self.place_in_area(light_wave, 'D3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.add(light_wave)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#00FFFF')
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Electrons emit secondary waves.",
            "These waves lag behind incident light.",
            "Interference creates resultant wave.",
            "This interaction slows phase velocity.",
            "Phase lag produces index refraction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Origin: Light-Matter Interaction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        atom = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/atom.svg")
        electron = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/electron.svg")
        
        # Elements
        incident_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#FFD700")
        
        # Adjust positioning based on feedback (Line 62, 63, 80, 91)
        self.place_in_area(incident_wave, 'A3', 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(atom, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(atom)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(electron, 'C5', 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(electron))
        secondary_wave = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#00BFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        secondary_wave.move_to(electron.get_center())
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(secondary_wave))
        self.play(secondary_wave.animate.scale(2).set_opacity(0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        # Visualization of lagging (simple phase shift)
        self.play(incident_wave.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        resultant_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.4 * np.sin(4 * x + 0.5), x_range=[-3, 3], color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(resultant_wave, 'D4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(resultant_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Indicate slower speed
        self.play(resultant_wave.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        label = Text("n > 1", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Lenses focus colors at differences.",
            "Chromatic aberration causes blur.",
            "Achromatic doublets correct color fringes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Chromatic Aberration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        lens = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lens.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(lens, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        sensor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sensor.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(sensor, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Rays
        ray_blue = Line(start=[-3, 1, 0], end=lens.get_center(), color='#0000FF')
        ray_red = Line(start=[-3, -1, 0], end=lens.get_center(), color='#FF0000')
        light_rays = VGroup(ray_blue, ray_red)
        
        # Focus points
        focus_blue = Dot(color='#0000FF').move_to(self.grid['B4'])
        focus_red = Dot(color='#FF0000').move_to(self.grid['B5'])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FFFF00')
        self.play(Create(lens), Create(light_rays))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(focus_blue),
            FadeIn(focus_red)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FFFF00')
        self.play(FadeIn(sensor))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#FFFF00')
        # Simulate correction
        self.play(
            focus_blue.animate.move_to(focus_red.get_center()),
            sensor.animate.move_to(focus_red.get_center())
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Harmonic Oscillator Model
sections.content: Briefly introduce the electron as a mass attached to the nucleus by a spring (Lorentz Oscillator Model). When an electromagnetic wave hits the electron, it begins to oscillate at the frequency of the incoming light.
sections.example: Visualize an electron as a ball connected to a spring; the incident light wave acts as a driving force pushing the ball back and forth.

sections.title: Origin: Light-Matter Interaction
sections.content: Explain that the index of refraction (n) arises from the phase lag between the incident light wave and the secondary waves emitted by the oscillating electrons. This interference reduces the phase velocity of the total wave.
sections.example: Animation showing the incident wave and the 'lagging' scattered waves overlapping to create a resultant wave with a slower phase velocity.

sections.title: Mechanism: Color Dependence (Dispersion)
sections.content: Introduce resonance frequency (ω₀). As the light frequency (color) approaches the natural resonance frequency of the electron-atom system, the phase lag changes drastically, causing the index of refraction to vary with color.
sections.example: A graph showing 'n' vs. 'wavelength'. Near the resonance peak, the curve shifts sharply, illustrating why blue light (higher frequency) bends more than red light in glass.

sections.title: Visualizing Dispersion: The Rainbow Effect
sections.content: Apply the concept to a prism. Because 'n' is color-dependent, different colors experience different phase velocities, leading to different angles of refraction (Snell's Law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂).
sections.example: A 'Rainbow Prism' animation: A white light beam enters a prism and splits into a spectrum, showing how each color follows a distinct path based on its unique 'n'.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Chromatic Aberration
sections.content: Summarize by linking the theory to a practical device: a camera lens. Explain that because blue and red light focus at different points, lenses must be corrected to prevent blurry, colored fringes.
sections.example: An animation of a 'Blurry vs. Sharp' image; showing how a multi-lens element system (Achromatic doublet) cancels out the color dependence to bring all colors to a single focal point.
